failure_modes.name: Missing_Evidence_Not_Specified
failure_modes.evidence: Summary_1 states 'To verify this claim, the following information is required: 1. **The identity and full details of the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham"** - specifically, who wrote this work and confirmation of any awards they received 2. **The nationality of the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham"** - whether this author was English or non-English' but does not name H. G. Wells explicitly as the missing entity to search for, leaving retrieval with only the book title.

failure_modes.name: Evidence_Present_But_Missed
failure_modes.evidence: Summary_1 claims 'they contain no information about the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham" or that author's nationality and awards' when passage [1] from hop 1 clearly states 'Love and Mr Lewisham... is a 1900 novel set in the 1880s by H. G. Wells.' The solver failed to identify H. G. Wells from passage [1] already available in hop 1.

failure_modes.name: Verdict_Despite_Insufficiency
failure_modes.evidence: Summary_2 renders verdict 'The claim is TRUE' and definitively states 'H. G. Wells, the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham," was English' without any passage confirming H. G. Wells was English or award-winning. The passages only identify Wells as the author but provide no nationality or award information.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Query hop 2: 'Who is the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham" and what is their nationality and major awards?' versus Query hop 3: 'Who was the award-winning author of "Love and Mr Lewisham" and what was their nationality?' Both queries ask nearly identical questions about the same book's author and nationality despite hop 2 already retrieving the author information.
